items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: there was WEBR that had jazz all the time with Joe Rico, who was a great jazz disc jockey at that

ctx.x: Without a question, yeah. Our house, my mother, God rest her soul, my mother was into jazz and so we grew up on listening to jazz all the time in the house although we didn’t get the stereo really until I was about oh I’d say six or seven years old, then we finally got a stereo. Otherwise it was the little radio. And we listened to jazz all the time. And then here in Buffalo we had Sunday afternoons there was “Sinatra and Strings,” there was WEBR that had jazz all the time with Joe Rico, who was a great jazz disc…

time, and so we always listened to jazz in the house and as my brothers got older, because I was the baby, as everybody got older we were introduced to a little bit of R&B type jazz, you know the Lou Rawls and things like that and those kind of things. But basically the context in the house was always jazz.
